messages.subject: missing data
parts:
in random effects models, such as the animal model (see previous post), a goal is often to estimate ("predict") random effects also for individuals without phenotypic records. This is possible via the known relationship/covariance to other individuals with phenotypic records. This is a missing data problem, but unlike the problem in section 6.1 of the manual, there are no observed predictors for the individuals without phenotypic record, so the solution given there does not apply, I think. What I did instead was:

data {
  int<lower=0> N_total; ## total number of individuals
  int<lower=0> N_phen; ## individuals with phenotypes
  real y[N_phen]; 
  matrix[N_total,N_total] A;
  vector[N_total] mu_u_prior;
}

parameters{
 ...
 vector[N_total] u;
...
} 


## likelihood loop runs only over individuals with records
for(i in 1:N_phen){                                      
       y[i] ~ normal(beta0 + u[i], sqrt(sigmasq_e)); 
     }  



The estimates of the individuals without record seem sensible. My question is, is this a correct approach.

Frank

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] missing data
parts:
That should work just fine. It won't be the most efficient, but until
we get sampling statements in the generated quantities block, it is
probably the best that can be done.

Cheers,
Marcus
